index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure illustrates the inference process of a Frame-Conditioned Video Generation (FCVG) model at time step t, structured as a symmetric, bidirectional denoising pipeline with temporal fusion. The global layout is horizontally oriented, progressing from left to right, with two parallel processing streams converging at a central fusion module. On the far left, two sets of noisy latent representations, labeled z_t^(1) through z_t^(N), are shown as stacked gray textured squares, representing N different latent states at time t. These are processed in two opposing directions: one stream flows upward from z_t^(1) to z_t^(N), while the other flows downward from z_t^(N) to z_t^(1), indicating forward and reverse temporal propagation. Each stream is associated with a conditional input: the top stream uses c_1→N, depicted as a stack of white squares containing multicolored skeletal motion trajectories, while the bottom stream uses c_N→1, similarly represented but corresponding to the reversed motion sequence. Both streams feed into separate instances of a 'Denoiser f_θ' module, which are rounded rectangles with dark blue borders and black text. These denoisers receive both the latent inputs and additional conditioning from two reference images: I_start (showing a person standing) and I_end (showing the same person in a dynamic pose), which are fed into the respective denoisers via vertical arrows. The outputs of the two denoisers converge at a circular 'Fusion' node, which combines them into a single output. This fused result is then passed to the right side of the diagram, where it is represented as a new set of latent states z_{t-1}^(1) through z_{t-1}^(N), again shown as stacked gray textured squares, indicating the denoised latent states at the previous time step t-1. A large, dark blue double-headed curved arrow labeled 'Time Reversal' connects the bottom denoiser to the fusion node, emphasizing the bidirectional nature of the process and the reversal of temporal order in the lower stream. All connections are indicated by thick black arrows, showing the flow of data from inputs to outputs. The overall structure reflects a time-reversible, frame-conditioned generative process where motion and image context guide the denoising of latent variables across time steps.
